data.node_interpretation: Each node is one internally isothermal lumped grain;the symmetric edge weight is the total contact thermal conductance,not conductivity or thermal resistance.

data.steady_state_model: At each internal node the net conductive heat flow is zero. Each contact has heat flow g_ij*(T_i-T_j);the two boundary node temperatures remain fixed. No heat source,radiation,convection or contact nonlinearity is included.
data.design_rule: Choose exactly one listed contact and add its conductance increment. Do not add increments to any other contact. Maximize the effective hot-to-cold conductance after all internal temperatures re-equilibrate. Candidate costs are equal;lexical contact ID resolves an exact tie.
data.reporting: Effective conductance is total heat leaving the hot boundary divided by its fixed temperature difference from the cold boundary. Report conductance W/K,not bulk thermal conductivity W/(m K);no specimen geometry is supplied.
data.scope: Controlled hypothetical grain/contact network. Contact values are model inputs,not measurements of a named material or a prediction from an atomistic force field.

provenance.kind: controlled computational analytical study, not experimental measurements
provenance.generation: Controlled computational input table for the stated study; not experimental measurements. Authentic source inputs are documented separately when present.
provenance.units: Contact and effective conductance W/K;temperature rise K;heat flowW;adjacency weights are conductances,not resistances. No spatial length is available to infer bulk conductivity.
